title: Never Meet Your No. 1 Fan; The Canadian Stage's Adaptation Of Stephen

display_heading.headline: Never Meet Your No. 1 Fan
display_heading.deck: The Canadian Stage's Adaptation Of Stephen King's Misery

contact_edits.before: Where the play and the actors excel is in giving life to the usually invisible bond between the oblivious entertainer and the audience who, in a mixture of grudge and gratitude, feels that she owns him and that he owes her. She, who for years has paid the piper, can finally make him dance to her tune. Each of them is comically oblivious of the other's values and modes of operation; they do know that they're in a life-and-death struggle. Rather less subtle are the setting that Britta Gerecke has dreamed up for Annie's stronghold, full of poles but short on walls, and James Fisher's supposedly spooky sound-score, which seems to think that the play is still a movie. The two forms have different ways of creating suspense, and what's effective in one can be ludicrous in the other. Which reminds me: The CanStage program note says Misery is the only work of King's to have made the journey from page to screen to stage. The writer must have forgotten the Broadway musical Carrie, a superflop so legendary a book was named after it. - Misery runs through May 31 at the Bluma Appel Theatre. Call 416-368-3110 for ticket details.
